attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-s4d1frtk/call-9c3eeb13015545d6a20e1bb90184c599/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la manuscript.pdf && readlink -f manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
for name in ['pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo','gs']:
 print(name, shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: EA-KD is simple and practically useful: it reweights existing distillation losses using teacher and student entropy, requires no auxiliary network, and supports both logit- and feature-based methods. Figure 1 indicates small computational overhead.

The classification evaluation is broad. Table 2 covers seven teacher–student pairs and multiple distillation frameworks, reporting average gains of 1.48 percentage points over vanilla KD and 0.56 points across all methods. Improvements also extend to Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet.
Transformer-to-CNN transfer, two COCO detector pairs, and supplementary language-model experiments provide useful evidence of applicability beyond the primary CIFAR-100 setting.

The paper acknowledges relevant adaptive and entropy-based distillation methods, provides component and temperature ablations, reports repeated-run variability in the supplement, and supplies a code link.
weaknesses: The experiments do not isolate sample prioritization from changes in overall distillation strength. The weights in Eqs. (9)–(14) are not normalized to unit mean, so they also change the balance between distillation and supervised learning. The MLD+LS coefficient adjustment from 9 to 4 illustrates this issue. Comparisons against a tuned constant weight and mean-normalized entropy weights are needed to establish what produces the gains.

The distinctive contribution of student-dependent weighting is only modestly supported. In Table 9, adding the student component improves teacher-only weighting from 75.14 to 75.46 for KD and from 78.30 to 78.38 for MLD+LS, while underperforming teacher-only weighting for FCFD. The gains over the closely related WTTM in Table A1 are only 0.03–0.19 points, with appreciable reported variability. These results leave the advantage of the proposed interaction over simpler existing weighting approaches uncertain.

The theoretical interpretation exceeds the analysis. Equations (5)–(7) compare extreme teacher distributions against a uniformly predicting student; they do not establish a general harmful bias throughout training. A small KL divergence can simply indicate agreement, and high predictive entropy does not necessarily imply useful label information. Likewise, t-SNE plots and loss-landscape slices are suggestive but do not establish the stronger decision-boundary and robustness claims.

Important implementation choices remain unspecified in the manuscript. In particular, whether gradients propagate through student entropy changes the objective: differentiating the weight introduces an additional entropy-gradient term. The aggregation of region or token entropies for detection and sequence-level language-model distillation also needs a precise definition.

Although the supplement reports standard deviations for EA variants, corresponding baseline variability is generally unavailable, limiting confidence in the smaller improvements over strong methods. Matched baseline reruns would strengthen these comparisons. Overall, the broad empirical gains make this a close decision, but the missing loss-scale controls and uncertain incremental benefit of the adaptive component support a slight preference for rejection.
